subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the vector equation of the plane passing through the line of intersection of the planes r·(i + j + k) = 6 and r·(2i + 3j + 4k) = −5 and through the point (1, 1, 1).

mark_split.label: Write both planes in the '= 0' form
Write the family through the line of intersection
Collect the normal and the constant
Substitute the point and find λ

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.81, chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Long Answer question 14. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+2+1+2+1+1 split weights the family of planes and the substitution that fixes λ, because those two moves are what the question is testing; the arithmetic that follows is one mark each. Paper position: Maths-1A Section C prints 3 long answers at 8 marks each and the student answers any 2; Product of Vectors is one of the units that can fill a Section-C slot. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find a plane through the line where two given planes meet and through a given point.

steps.label: Write both planes as = 0
steps.margin_note: First mark. Move each constant to the left first. The family in the next step only works when both planes are written with zero on the right.
steps.memory_tip: Move both constants left first. The family needs zero on the right of each plane.

recall.must_convey: That both planes are rewritten with zero on the right, as r·(i + j + k) − 6 = 0 and r·(2i + 3j + 4k) + 5 = 0.
accept: write both planes with zero on the right hand side
move the six and the minus five across
the second becomes r dot two i plus three j plus four k plus five equals zero
rendu planes ni equals zero form lo rasta
put both equations in the equals zero form first

steps.why: The combination used in the next step adds the two left-hand sides, so both have to be expressions that are zero on the plane.
common_mistakes: Leaving the second plane as r·n = −5, so the sign of the 5 is lost.
Changing a sign inside the normal while moving the constant.

steps.label: Write the family
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Any point on the line of intersection makes both brackets zero, so it makes the combination zero for every λ. That is why this expression is a plane through the line.
steps.memory_tip: On the line both brackets are zero, so the combination is zero for every λ.

recall.must_convey: That any plane through the line of intersection has the form (1) + λ(2) = 0, because every point of the line makes both brackets zero.

every point of the line makes both brackets zero so the combination is zero
the family of planes through the line is one plus lambda two

use the family with one unknown lambda

steps.why: The planes through a fixed line form one family with a single unknown λ, and the extra point selects one member of that family.
common_mistakes: Multiplying the two plane equations instead of adding them.
Putting λ on both brackets, which just scales the whole equation.

steps.label: Collect the terms
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Gather the r terms into one dot product and move the constants to the right. The normal now depends on λ.
steps.memory_tip: Gather the r terms into ONE dot product; the normal now depends on λ.

accept: collect the r terms into one dot product with the normal depending on lambda
the normal is one plus two lambda, one plus three lambda, one plus four lambda
the right hand side is six minus five lambda
r terms ni okate dot product ga collect chesta
write it as r dot something equals six minus five lambda

steps.why: Writing the family in r·n = d form is what makes the next substitution a single line of arithmetic in λ.
common_mistakes: Leaving +5λ on the right instead of −5λ.
Adding the two normals without the λ factor on the second.

steps.label: Find λ
steps.margin_note: Two marks. The point (1, 1, 1) has position vector i + j + k, and dotting it with the normal simply adds the three brackets.
steps.memory_tip: For the point (1, 1, 1) the dot product is just the SUM of the three brackets.
lines: put r = i + j + k in (3) :

recall.must_convey: That substituting r = i + j + k gives 3 + 9λ = 6 − 5λ, so λ = 3/14.

three plus nine lambda equals six minus five lambda

substitute the point and solve the linear equation for lambda

steps.why: The point is the extra condition that selects one plane from the family, and it gives a linear equation in λ with a single solution.
common_mistakes: Dotting the point with the wrong side of equation (3).

steps.label: Put λ back
steps.margin_note: Seventh mark. Keep everything over 14 rather than turning it into decimals — the fractions all clear in the next line.
steps.memory_tip: Keep everything over 14. The fourteens all clear in the next line.

recall.must_convey: That putting λ = 3/14 back gives the normal (20i + 23j + 26k)/14 and the constant 69/14.
accept: put lambda back to get twenty, twenty three, twenty six all over fourteen
the constant is six minus fifteen over fourteen which is sixty nine over fourteen

steps.why: Working in fourteenths keeps every number a whole number on top, and the common factor of 14 disappears when the equation is multiplied through.
common_mistakes: Turning 3/14 into a decimal and losing exactness.
Forgetting the 1 that sits in front of each bracket.

steps.label: Write the plane
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Multiplying by 14 clears every fraction. The point check is one addition and confirms the whole calculation.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply by 14 to clear the fractions, then check the point in one addition.

recall.must_convey: That multiplying by 14 gives r·(20i + 23j + 26k) = 69, and that (1, 1, 1) satisfies it.
accept: multiply by fourteen to get r dot twenty i plus twenty three j plus twenty six k equals sixty nine

steps.why: Multiplying a plane equation by a non-zero number gives the same plane, so clearing the 14 changes nothing but makes the answer readable.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer with fourteenths in it.
Multiplying only the left-hand side by 14.
